format: Independent shop billing statement, parts and labour, handwritten-style layout
why: The cleanest possible reconciliation test. Seven priced lines that sum to exactly the printed total of 3,325.00, so any dropped or misread line is provable rather than suspected.

It carries its own OCR error to catch: REPLACE THERMOSTAT prints as '350.¢' rather than 350.00. Read literally the lines sum to 2,975.00 against a printed 3,325.00, and the 350.00 gap is exactly the mangled line. This is what F4 exists to detect.

Textbook PART versus OPERATION separation. The same three nouns appear twice, once as a part and once prefixed REPLACE as the labour. An extractor that cannot tell them apart will double-count the components or the money.

Page 2 is not a receipt at all. It is a screenshot of a body-composition scale that the owner uploaded by mistake — 'STATE OF Health', 'BLD T laiararata', a percentage and a time. Nothing from it may reach any field. This is the strongest available test of the prompt's boilerplate and noise rejection.
Shop name OCRs as 'GTA Auio Services' rather than 'GTA Auto Services' in four runs out of five, which is why shopName is scored by similarity and not exact match.
redacted: plate number in the vehicle line
kept: shop name and branch, including the Auio/Auto OCR error, which is the point of the fuzzy shopName rule
notes: OCR came from the earlier Tesseract provider, not Google Vision. Kept deliberately: it is noisier than Vision output and a set of only clean text would flatter the extractor.

relatedComponents is a judgement call worth revisiting. A distributor condenser is an ignition component, so it is filed under Electrical rather than AC System; the temperature sensor and thermostat are Cooling System. A reviewer may argue Engine belongs here too.
